findings.problem: QuoteWorkflow has no typestate enum or state machine. Any combination of status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms is representable.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct impossible domain states such as is_sent=true with is_validated=false, or status="sent" with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, violating make-illegal-states-unrepresentable.
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms with a single QuoteStatus enum (e.g., QuoteStatus::Draft, DraftValidated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }) and make QuoteWorkflow hold only the enum.

findings.problem: pub status: String allows any arbitrary string value. No smart constructor or enum restricts domain states.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set status to any value ("deleted", "banana", "SENT", "") and there is no compile-time guarantee the workflow is in a valid lifecycle stage.
findings.fix: Replace with pub status: QuoteStatus where QuoteStatus is an enum with exhaustive variants (Draft, Validated, Sent). Remove all lifecycle booleans.

findings.problem: pub is_validated: bool and pub is_sent: bool are independent booleans that encode a lifecycle. Combined with status: String they form an ambiguous, inconsistent state machine.
findings.failure_mode: The struct represents contradictory states: status="draft" with is_sent=true, or status="sent" with is_validated=false. No single function or type enforces valid transitions.
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single typestate enum. Each variant owns the fields it needs (e.g., Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }).

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a dangling Option that is independent of the sent lifecycle boolean. It can be Some without is_sent=true, or is_sent=true without Some timestamp.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can create states where a quote is sent but has no timestamp, or has a timestamp but is not marked sent. The Option does not belong to a variant that owns it.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the typestate enum variant: Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }. The timestamp becomes required and owned by the Sent variant, eliminating Option entirely.

findings.problem: pub id: String is a raw primitive with no domain identity rules, no format constraints, no newtype wrapper.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set id to empty string, whitespace, or invalid UUIDs. There is no compile-time distinction between a quote ID and any other string, enabling accidental mixing of identifiers.
findings.fix: Introduce QuoteId newtype: pub struct QuoteId(String); with a smart constructor that validates format (e.g., UUID regex) and returns a typed error on invalid input.

findings.problem: The struct is pub with all fields pub. There is no parse boundary — raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can create a QuoteWorkflow with arbitrary status strings, inconsistent boolean combinations, and invalid IDs without any validation, defeating domain invariants.
findings.fix: Make QuoteWorkflow struct private with private fields. Provide a single smart constructor or builder that takes parsed domain types (QuoteId, QuoteStatus) and validates invariants. All external input must flow through parse functions at crate boundaries.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs heap allocation via "sent".to_string() inside what should be a pure typestate transition. The function mutates status string instead of transitioning an enum variant.
findings.failure_mode: Every call to mark_sent allocates a new String on the heap, increasing memory traffic and allocation cost. The function cannot be const or zero-cost, and the string mutation prevents the compiler from proving state invariants.
findings.fix: Replace with a pure typestate transition: fn mark_sent(item: QuoteWorkflow) -> QuoteWorkflow { QuoteWorkflow { status: QuoteStatus::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: now_epoch_ms() }, ..item } } where QuoteStatus::Sent owns its timestamp and no heap allocation occurs for the state change.

findings.problem: No try_reserve or bounded allocation strategy exists anywhere in the crate. The QuoteWorkflow struct itself has no capacity management, and mark_sent has no bounded allocation pattern.
findings.failure_mode: While not immediately critical for this small struct, the absence of try_reserve and domain caps means any future Vec/string collection in the crate lacks allocation discipline, risking unbounded heap growth.
findings.fix: Validate a domain cap/max before any Vec::new().call to try_reserve(cap).map_err(|_| AllocationError)? pattern. Add a domain-level item cap constant.

findings.problem: No benchmarks, profiler data, or allocation evidence exist for mark_sent or any hot path.
findings.failure_mode: Without benchmark/baseline evidence, performance claims cannot be verified. The heap allocation in mark_sent on line 10 cannot be measured or proven acceptable.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or simple benchmark comparing the current String-based mark_sent against a typestate-enum version to measure allocation delta.

residual_risk: Static review only — no commands were run per eval sandbox rules. The crate has 6 BLOCKER findings all centered on the absence of typestate enums, status strings, independent lifecycle booleans, and a parse boundary. The structural fix (replace struct fields with a QuoteStatus typestate enum and QuoteId newtype, make struct private with smart constructor) is well understood and straightforward. Residual risk is low once the typestate refactor lands, but remains BLOCKER-level until implemented.
